title: intent agents sync writes each declared language's default build and test commands into AGENTS.md, which are wrong for a project that builds another way
body:
**`intent agents sync` WRITES EACH DECLARED LANGUAGE'S DEFAULT BUILD AND TEST COMMANDS INTO AGENTS.md, AND NOTHING A PROJECT DECLARES CAN CHANGE THEM, SO A PROJECT THAT BUILDS OR TESTS ANOTHER WAY GETS A CONTRACT THAT NAMES THE WRONG COMMANDS.**

**Seen in four projects, and across the fleet by survey.**

- **Ccusage**, raised by ccusage-vc at hv's request on 2026-11-03. Ccusage declares `rust` and `shell`. After `intent agents sync` under 3.2.8 (Ccusage 80179a5), its AGENTS.md lists "Bats testing framework" as a prerequisite, `cargo test` and `bats -r tests/` as its test commands, and `cargo build` as its build. Ccusage has no Bats tests: its shell test is `sh tests/release.sh`, and every cargo command its checks run takes `--locked`. Its workaround (41eb982) points usage-rules.md at README's Development section and docs/releasing.md, and says that AGENTS.md's Bats and unlocked cargo lines are Intent's generic text. Ccusage vendors devbin 0.1.19 since 2026-11-03, and declaring its own commands is Ccusage ISSUE:0006. Re-measured by intent-vc on 2026-11-06: since b1cb3e3 (2026-11-03 12:53Z by git's UTC date) Ccusage keeps a Bats suite of five files under `tests/`, which its usage-rules.md runs as `bin/devbin test shell`, so "no Bats tests" held at 80179a5 and does not now. Its AGENTS.md still lists `bats -r tests/` and the unlocked cargo lines.
- **Trellis**, raised by trellis-vc on hv's word ("That's a bug. Raise it with devbin-vc and we'll sort it out over there"), received before 2026-11-01 14:00Z by date -u and carried to intent-vc on devbin-vc's board (Devbin todo 192). Trellis declares `swift` and `content`. With `swift` declared, the template renders a `Package.swift` prerequisite and `swift build` and `swift test`, but Trellis's Swift is one Xcode project, `native/ios/Trellis.xcodeproj`, built through `bin/devbin build` and tested with `xcodebuild test`. Trellis carries a hand correction (6f9200f) that its next `intent agents sync` will revert.
- **Intent itself**, measured by intent-vc on 2026-11-03. Intent declares `elixir`, `author`, `content`, `rust`, `shell` and `swift`, and its AGENTS.md names `mix.exs` and `Package.swift` as where the toolchain versions live and lists `mix deps.get`, `mix compile`, `mix test`, `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `swift build`, `swift test` and `bats -r tests/`. The tree has no `mix.exs`, `Package.swift` or `Cargo.toml` at its root. The Rust workspace is `native/rust/Cargo.toml`, the Swift is the Xcode project `native/macos/Intent/Intent.xcodeproj`, and the Linux preflight, which mirrors CI, builds with `cargo build --release --manifest-path native/rust/Cargo.toml` and tests with `cd tests && ./run_tests.sh`.
- **Webber**, raised by webber-dc on hv's word on 2026-11-06 and sent to intent-vc directly, in the session hv started to receive it (received by 11:26Z by intent-vc's date -u); checked against Webber's tree by intent-vc the same day. Webber was made on 2026-11-06 under Intent 3.2.8 (webber-dc gives 04:25Z; its first commit, 399e5eb, is at 04:31Z by git's UTC date) and declares `swift` and `shell`. Its AGENTS.md lists a Swift toolchain prerequisite that points at `Package.swift`, "Bats testing framework", `swift build` under Setup and under Building, and `swift test` and `bats -r tests/` under Test commands. With `swift` and `shell` its only languages, these are the only build and test lines it has. Webber has no `Package.swift`: its Swift is one Xcode project, `native/ios/Webber.xcodeproj`, built and tested through `bin/devbin`, with the `xcodebuild` lines and the build stamps in `bin/build-app`, and its Bats runs as `bin/devbin test shell`. Webber's usage-rules.md overrides the lines ("Never run `xcodebuild`, `swift build`, `swift test` or `bats` directly, whatever `AGENTS.md` lists for the declared languages"). On hv's word the same day ("Fix it here now and let intent-vc know what you did", relayed by webber-dc), Webber carries a stopgap paragraph in CLAUDE.md, under the line the template preserves across regeneration: 7cf25e1, on Webber's main by 11:31Z by intent-vc's date -u. It says that Webber is an Xcode project, that AGENTS.md's `swift build`, `swift test` and `bats -r tests/` lines come from Intent's template and do not apply (this issue), and that every build and test goes only through `bin/devbin`, in a slot the estate's controller has granted.

**The fleet**, surveyed by webber-dc on 2026-11-06 and re-measured by intent-vc the same day, by reads only, over the 20 Intent projects under `~/Devel/prj` on rhadamanth:

- Ten declare `swift`: Baize, Conflab, Gtools, Intent, Lamplight, Pplr, Prolix, Trellis, Utilz and Webber. None has a `Package.swift` at its root. Eight keep their Swift in an Xcode project: Prolix (`native/ios/Prolix.xcodeproj`), Lamplight (`native/ios/Storyfield/Storyfield.xcodeproj`), Conflab (`native/macos/Conflab/Conflab.xcodeproj`, from a project.yml), Gtools (`native/macos/Gtools/Gtools.xcodeproj`, from a project.yml), Utilz (`native/macos/Menuz/Menuz.xcodeproj`, from a project.yml), Intent, Trellis and Webber. Baize's only Swift is one generated file, `apps/rack/priv/tokens/generated/Tokens.swift`, and Pplr's is two standalone scripts, `swift/fold-table/main.swift` and `swift/pplr-contacts/main.swift`; neither has a package or an Xcode project.
- Nine of the ten carry the template's `swift build` and `swift test` lines. Trellis carries its hand correction, which the next sync reverts: `lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md` has no preserved block, where `_CLAUDE.md` has one.
- Two `Package.swift` files exist under `~/Devel/prj`, and neither is at an Intent project's root: Utilz's `native/macos/Menuz/MenuzKit/Package.swift`, a package inside the Menuz Xcode project, and Arca's `arca_swift/Package.swift` (Arca is not an Intent project). webber-dc's survey counted the eight projects that keep Swift in an Xcode project, and named Arca's as the only `Package.swift`.
- The `shell` block's `bats -r tests/` is in 17 of the 20 AGENTS.md files. The three without it are Prodinfra, which declares no language, Riffle, which declares only `elixir`, and Trellis. In 11 of the 17, `tests/` holds no `.bats` file: Cdtempl and Molt keep theirs in `test/`, Utilz under `opt/`, and Anvil, Baize, Cldr, Gtools, Laksa, Lamplight, MicroGPTEx and Prolix have none outside devbin's vendored `bin/.devbin/`.
- 19 of the 20 have `bin/devbin`. Anvil does not.

**What the wrong lines cost.** All 20 projects' CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md (`@AGENTS.md`), so these lines are in the context of every Claude Code session in them. None imports usage-rules.md, which is where Webber and Ccusage put their overrides, so an override reaches only a session that goes and reads it. And under the estate rule webber-dc reports from hv on 2026-11-06, which Webber's usage-rules.md also states, every build or test runs in a slot the estate's controller grants (devbin-vc has held the controller since 06:52Z, by `intent estate status`). A session that follows one of these lines therefore runs the wrong command and also starts an unbooked heavy run on a shared host.

**Triage**, by intent-vc on 2026-11-06, which hv asked for: severity raised from medium to high. The `swift` lines are wrong in nine of the ten projects that declare `swift`, and `bats -r tests/` finds no test file in 11 of the 17 projects whose AGENTS.md lists it. The contract is imported into every session in those projects and the overrides are not. The one correction found, Trellis's, is reverted by the next sync. Following a line is an unbooked heavy run under the estate's slot rule. It is not critical: it corrupts no data and blocks no release.

**Where it comes from.** `lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md` carries a fixed block per language (`[[#lang <lang>]]`), each holding that language's default prerequisites and build and test commands, and its only substitutions are `[[PROJECT_NAME]]` and `[[INTENT_VERSION]]`. `intent/.config/config.json` has no key for a project's own build and test commands. A hand edit cannot hold: in-essentials forbids it, the next `intent agents sync` overwrites it, and Ccusage's `.claude/settings.json` denies `Edit(/AGENTS.md)`.

**Fix options**, from ccusage-vc's report and hv's framing that in this estate devbin is how projects build and test, not Intent:

1. When the project has `bin/devbin`, the template points at it for building and testing.
2. A project declares its own build and test commands, and the template renders them.
3. The template drops the language-default commands, since it cannot know a project's own.

intent-vc's recommendation: render the build and test lines from what the project declares, in that order of preference: `bin/devbin` when the tree has one, else declared commands, else no build or test lines at all. A language default is right only by coincidence. Every project above and every project in the survey that declares `swift` has `bin/devbin`, so the first option alone would correct each of those cases, which is webber-dc's point, measured. It is not the whole fix: Anvil declares `shell` and `elixir` and has no `bin/devbin`, so the rest of the order is what reaches it. Pointing at `bin/devbin` corrects the command, not the booking: Webber's usage-rules.md says its vendored devbin asks for no slot itself, so the contract would still have to say that a heavy run is booked with the estate's controller. Two projects cite this issue in their own files and change once it is fixed: Webber's CLAUDE.md paragraph (7cf25e1) comes out once the template renders `bin/devbin`, and Ccusage's usage-rules.md names this issue as the source of its AGENTS.md's Bats and unlocked cargo lines.

**Sizing and delivery**, read by intent-vc from the source and the install on 2026-11-06:

- **A template-only fix is S.** The per-language lines under Setup, Test commands and Building give way to one paragraph that sends the reader to the project's own commands, through `bin/devbin` where the tree has one and otherwise to what its README or usage-rules.md names, and to the estate's controller for a slot where `intent estate status` shows one. The "see `Package.swift`" prerequisite and the "Run the test suite before making changes" step change with it. It needs no renderer change: `init_from_empty_dir.rs` pins the shell prerequisite line, and `agents_sync_parity.rs` asserts structure, not bytes. Its cost is that the template names devbin to every Intent user, whether or not the project has it.
- **The recommended shape is M.** `rootfiles::substitute` is pure and sees no file system, and its blocks do not nest, so rendering devbin lines only where `bin/devbin` exists needs a fact passed in from its five call sites, a new block kind and tests. Declared commands, option 2, add a config key and a verb to set it.
- **A fix on main reaches no project by itself.** Brew's `intent` renders AGENTS.md from its keg (`INTENT_HOME` is `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/intent/3.2.8/libexec`, whose `_AGENTS.md` is byte-identical to main's), so a fix reaches a project at the next cut and that project's next `intent agents sync`. Until then, the protection that works is a paragraph in the project's CLAUDE.md preserved block, as in Webber's 7cf25e1.

**Recorded only.** hv's word, relayed by ccusage-vc on 2026-11-03, is that this is not fixed today; the filing is on hv's go, relayed the same way. On 2026-11-06 hv asked intent-vc to triage the issue and update this record with webber-dc's report, then asked what a fix would take, and banked it for 2026-11-07 ("we need to bank this and come back to it tomorrow"); no fix is ruled.


**The shape narrowed on 2026-11-10** (vc's ruling under hv's pen, replacing the "full shape, M" ruling): the fix is the devbin case alone. AGENTS.md says a project builds and tests through `bin/devbin` where its tree has one, with the estate controller's slot first, and otherwise that it declares no build or test commands, pointing at its README and `usage-rules.md`; no language default survives. Declared commands, the recommendation's middle step, need a config key and a verb to set it, and `intent config set` is declared and unimplemented (its help says it exits 2), so they would have taken the package past M. They are an addition rather than this defect, and are issue 0678, not built; whether 0678 rides 3.3.0 is hv's. Built by ic as refs/bank/ic/0672/fix-v1-on-0650v2, for vc's judgement.
